families.title: Air-Liquid Heat Exchanger
families.summary: Transfers heat between an air system and a liquid system, with five named size variants.
families.body: An air-liquid heat exchanger transfers heat between an air circuit and a liquid circuit, bringing their temperatures toward one another. The family has five size variants. Heat exchange is described as proportional to component size, and all five variants have the same air, liquid and temperature connections.

sections.title: Connections and temperature outputs
sections.body: Air In and Air Out connect the air circuit. Fluid In and Fluid Out connect the liquid circuit. Temp A reports compartment air temperature, while Temp B reports compartment water temperature. The liquid-side reading retains the more specific water wording used in the port description. Both readings describe compartments rather than explicitly identified inlet or outlet temperatures.

sections.title: Heat exchange between circuits
sections.body: The exchanger averages heat between the air and liquid systems. Its role is to exchange heat between those systems; either circuit can be the one being cooled. Each circuit has its own inlet and outlet pair, with a temperature output for each compartment.

sections.title: Size variants
sections.body: The five variants are 1x2, 5x2, 5x3, 9x3 and 9x5. Their definition masses are 2, 7, 45, 81 and 225, and their definition values are 15, 30, 50, 80 and 150, respectively. Their listed voxel counts are 2, 10, 45, 81 and 225. These counts describe the component definitions separately from the size names. For example, the 5x3 variant lists 45 voxels.

families.title: Blinker
families.summary: The blinker outputs a value that blinks between on and off at a set rate.
families.body: You can set the duration that the signal should stay on and off for by selecting it with the select tool. A control signal determines whether or not the blinker should output anything. If the control signal is off, the blinker's output will be off. The internal blink timer is reset every time the control signal is switched off.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Control Signal: Controls whether or not the blinker should output anything at all.

Blinking Signal: Outputs a signal that blinks between on and off at the set rate when the control signal is on. Outputs off if the control signal is off.

families.title: Compact Pilot Seat
families.summary: The compact pilot seat lets you translate keyboard presses into output signals that can control logic components.
families.body: It provides 4 number outputs that produce a standard value ranging from -1 to 1, and 6 on/off outputs. You can get in and out of the compact pilot seat by interacting with it using [$[action_use_seat]].

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Occupied: Outputs an on signal if this seat is occupied by a character.

Trigger [$[action_trigger]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_trigger]] is held, and off when it is not.

Look X: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the X-axis.

Look Y: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the Y-axis.

Axis 1 [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_left]] and [$[action_right]]. [$[action_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 2 [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_up]] and [$[action_down]]. [$[action_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_up]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 3 [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_pedal_left]] and [$[action_pedal_right]]. [$[action_pedal_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_pedal_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 4 [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_throttle_up]] and [$[action_throttle_down]]. [$[action_throttle_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_throttle_up]] moves it towards 1.

Hotkey 1 [$[action_hotkey_1]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_1]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 2 [$[action_hotkey_2]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_2]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 3 [$[action_hotkey_3]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_3]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 4 [$[action_hotkey_4]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_4]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 5 [$[action_hotkey_5]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_5]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 6 [$[action_hotkey_6]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_6]] is held, and off when it is not.

Seat data: Outputs the axis, hotkey and occupied data from the seat. (On/Off 1+ : Hotkeys) (On/Off 31 : Trigger) (On/Off 32 : Occupied) (Value 1 : [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]) (Value 2 : [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]) (Value 3 : [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]) (Value 4 : [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]) (Value 9 : Look X)  (Value 10 : Look Y)

Headset Audio: Label only; no description is supplied.

Headset Video: Displays video UI overlay on a helmet mounted display.

families.title: Control Handle
families.summary: A compact control handle.
families.body: You can get in and out of the position by interacting with it using [$[action_use_seat]].

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Occupied: Outputs an on signal if the handle is occupied by a character.

Trigger [$[action_trigger]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_trigger]] is held, and off when it is not.

Look X: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the X-axis.

Look Y: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the Y-axis.

Axis 1 [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_left]] and [$[action_right]]. [$[action_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 2 [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_up]] and [$[action_down]]. [$[action_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_up]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 3 [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_pedal_left]] and [$[action_pedal_right]]. [$[action_pedal_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_pedal_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 4 [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_throttle_up]] and [$[action_throttle_down]]. [$[action_throttle_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_throttle_up]] moves it towards 1.

Hotkey 1 [$[action_hotkey_1]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_1]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 2 [$[action_hotkey_2]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_2]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 3 [$[action_hotkey_3]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_3]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 4 [$[action_hotkey_4]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_4]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 5 [$[action_hotkey_5]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_5]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 6 [$[action_hotkey_6]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_6]] is held, and off when it is not.

Seat data: Outputs the axis, hotkey and occupied data from the helm. (On/Off 1+ : Hotkeys) (On/Off 31 : Trigger) (On/Off 32 : Occupied) (Value 1 : [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]) (Value 2 : [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]) (Value 3 : [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]) (Value 4 : [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]) (Value 9 : Look X)  (Value 10 : Look Y)

Headset Audio: Label only; no description is supplied.

Headset Video: Displays video UI overlay on a helmet mounted display.

families.title: Dial
families.summary: A dial with a rotating needle for displaying numerical values.
families.body: The dial's face represents values ranging from -1 to 1 by default. This can be configured by selecting it with the select tool. families.title: Diesel Engine
families.summary: Self-contained small, medium and large diesel engines with fuel, air, coolant and exhaust connections.
families.body: Throttle accepts 0 to 1. Starter uses electricity to increase engine RPS during startup. Fuel and Air supply the engine; In Coolant is the cold return and Out Coolant is the hot output. Exhaust removes combustion fumes. Separate data outputs report RPS and temperature. The mechanical port is also labelled RPS, so its role must be read from its description rather than the label alone.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Throttle: Standard value between 0 and 1 that controls the throttle of the engine.

Starter: Increases the engine RPS using electrical power to start up the engine.

RPS: The power supplied by the engine for inputting to other components.

Fuel: The fuel supply for the engine.

Air: The air supply for the engine.

In Coolant: The return flow (cold) for the coolant system.

Out Coolant: The output flow (hot) for the coolant system.

Exhaust: Out flow for combusted fumes from the engine.

RPS: Output value giving data info on engine speed.

Temperature: Output value giving data info on engine temperature.

Electric: Electrical power connection.

families.title: Driver seat
families.summary: The driver seat lets you translate keyboard presses into output signals that can control logic components.
families.body: It provides 4 number outputs that produce a standard value ranging from -1 to 1, and 6 on/off outputs. You can get in and out of the driver seat by interacting with it using [$[action_use_seat]].

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Occupied: Outputs an on signal if this seat is occupied by a character.

Trigger [$[action_trigger]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_trigger]] is held, and off when it is not.

Look X: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the X-axis.

Look Y: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the Y-axis.

Axis 1 [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_left]] and [$[action_right]]. [$[action_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 2 [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_up]] and [$[action_down]]. [$[action_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_up]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 3 [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_pedal_left]] and [$[action_pedal_right]]. [$[action_pedal_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_pedal_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 4 [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_throttle_up]] and [$[action_throttle_down]]. [$[action_throttle_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_throttle_up]] moves it towards 1.

Hotkey 1 [$[action_hotkey_1]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_1]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 2 [$[action_hotkey_2]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_2]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 3 [$[action_hotkey_3]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_3]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 4 [$[action_hotkey_4]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_4]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 5 [$[action_hotkey_5]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_5]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 6 [$[action_hotkey_6]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_6]] is held, and off when it is not.

Seat data: Outputs the axis, hotkey and occupied data from the seat. (On/Off 1+ : Hotkeys) (On/Off 31 : Trigger) (On/Off 32 : Occupied) (Value 1 : [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]) (Value 2 : [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]) (Value 3 : [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]) (Value 4 : [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]) (Value 9 : Look X)  (Value 10 : Look Y)

Headset Audio: Label only; no description is supplied.

Headset Video: Displays video UI overlay on a helmet mounted display.

families.title: Electric Fluid Pump
families.summary: Moves fluid between an inlet and outlet under on/off control.
families.body: An electric fluid pump moves fluid through a vehicle's fluid system. Fluid In takes fluid into the pump and Fluid Out releases it. Electric supplies power, On/Off controls pumping, and Flow Rate reports flow in L/s. The small and large variants have pump_pressure configuration values of 10 and 100.

Fluid In: Connect to an inlet component to take fluid into the system.

Fluid Out: Connect to an outlet component to release fluid from the system.

Electric: Electrical power connection.

Flow Rate: Fluid flow rate in L/s.

On/Off: Controls whether or not the fluid is being pumped.

families.title: Gas Meter
families.summary: A device to measure how much gas is within an enclosed volume.
families.body: This will output a quantity in litres and the total capacity in litres.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Gas Level: Returns the number of litres of gas in an enclosed volume.

Fluid Capacity: Returns the total capacity of an enclosed volume in litres, or 0 if not enclosed.

Composite Data: Outputs the volumes of individual gas types on their respective channel. The data can be directly merged with a Liquid meter. The Air fluid type is equivalent to the sum of the oxygen, carbon dioxide and nitrogen values. Channels: 4-Air, 5-CO2, 8-Steam, 11-Oxygen, 12-Nitrogen, 13-Hydrogen.

families.title: Gyro
families.summary: The gyroscope takes 4 standard value signals representing the desired yaw, pitch, roll and vertical motion of a helicopter.
families.body: It outputs stabilised values that can be sent to rotors and engines to make them much easier to control. An on/off input allows you to activate and deactivate the internal auto-hover circuit. When auto-hover is enabled, the gyroscope will attempt to keep your helicopter steady.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Roll: Accepts a standard value between -1 and 1 representing the desired roll speed.

Stabilised Roll: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1 representing a stabilised roll speed.

Pitch: Accepts a standard value between -1 and 1 representing the desired pitch speed.

Stabilised Pitch: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1 representing a stabilised pitch speed.

Yaw: Accepts a standard value between -1 and 1 representing the desired yaw speed.

Stabilised Yaw: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1 representing a stabilised yaw speed.

Up/Down: Accepts a standard value between -1 and 1 representing the desired vertical speed.

Stabilised Up/Down: Outputs a standard value between 0 and 1 representing a stabilised upward thrust.

Auto-hover: Enables the gyroscope's auto-hover circuit when receiving an on signal.

Electric: Electrical power connection.

families.title: Harness
families.summary: A rescue harness.
families.body: You can get in and out of the harness by interacting with it using [$[action_use_seat]]. You can place a rescued survivor in any harness by using [$[action_use_seat]] while carrying them.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Occupied: Outputs an on signal if this harness is occupied by a character.

Trigger [$[action_trigger]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_trigger]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 1 [$[action_hotkey_1]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_1]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 2 [$[action_hotkey_2]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_2]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 3 [$[action_hotkey_3]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_3]] is held, and off when it is not.

Seat Data: Outputs the axis, hotkey and occupied data from the seat. (On/Off 1+ : Hotkeys) (On/Off 31 : Trigger) (On/Off 32 : Occupied) (Value 1 : [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]) (Value 2 : [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]) (Value 3 : [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]) (Value 4 : [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]])

families.title: Helm
families.summary: A steering helm with steering wheel.
families.body: You can get in and out of the position by interacting with it using [$[action_use_seat]]. You can place a rescued survivor in any position by using [$[action_use_seat]] while carrying them.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Occupied: Outputs an on signal if the helm is occupied by a character.

Trigger [$[action_trigger]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_trigger]] is held, and off when it is not.

Look X: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the X-axis.

Look Y: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the Y-axis.

Axis 1 [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_left]] and [$[action_right]]. [$[action_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 2 [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_up]] and [$[action_down]]. [$[action_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_up]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 3 [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_pedal_left]] and [$[action_pedal_right]]. [$[action_pedal_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_pedal_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 4 [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_throttle_up]] and [$[action_throttle_down]]. [$[action_throttle_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_throttle_up]] moves it towards 1.

Hotkey 1 [$[action_hotkey_1]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_1]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 2 [$[action_hotkey_2]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_2]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 3 [$[action_hotkey_3]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_3]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 4 [$[action_hotkey_4]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_4]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 5 [$[action_hotkey_5]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_5]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 6 [$[action_hotkey_6]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_6]] is held, and off when it is not.

Seat data: Outputs the axis, hotkey and occupied data from the helm. (On/Off 1+ : Hotkeys) (On/Off 31 : Trigger) (On/Off 32 : Occupied) (Value 1 : [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]) (Value 2 : [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]) (Value 3 : [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]) (Value 4 : [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]) (Value 9 : Look X)  (Value 10 : Look Y)

Headset Audio: Label only; no description is supplied.

Headset Video: Displays video UI overlay on a helmet mounted display.

families.title: Hose
families.summary: A building block attached to the end of a mechanical hose that can be raised and lowered.
families.body: This can be used to transport water between Two bodies. Two on/off signals are used to control whether the hose is moving up (towards the base) or down (away from the base). A number output allows you to measure the hose's current length if necessary. The maximum length of the hose is 16 metres (64 blocks). The speed of the hose mechanism can be configured by selecting this component with the select tool.

families.title: Instrument Panel
families.summary: A customisable panel that can have up to 4 different instruments, controlled by a composite signal from a microcontroller.
families.body: The 4 instruments can be selected in the properties window. Each type of instrument has options for choosing the composite channels that they read from or write to. Composite signals are bridged from the input node to the output node to enable displays to be chained together. Instruments marked as '(On/Off)' require multiple on/off signals to control each of their segments individually.

families.title: Keel
families.summary: A small boat keel used for sailing.
families.body: The keel resists rolling forces while submerged, helping to keep a boat upright and stable. The keel also resists lateral sliding forces, causing the majority of a boats movement to be in the direction of the keel axis. When combined with the force provided by a sail, this allows a sailboat to move forward in a crosswind, or even upwind.

families.body: Two large connectors will attach when they are within close proximity and both are switched on. families.title: Laser Point Sensor
families.summary: A sensor that outputs a relative x and y position of a laser point that it can see within its field of view.
families.body: The closest point to the center of the sensor's field of view will be reported. It outputs a value of -1 to 1 on composite number channel 1 for the x position, and a value of -1 to 1 on composite number channel 2 for the y position. Composite on/off channel 1 is set to on when a point is visible. The -1 to 1 values map to an fov of -cos(0.5) to cos(0.5) in both the x and y directions.

families.title: Linear Track Base
families.summary: A slider that moves along a modular linear track.
families.body: You can build the track using the Linear Track Extension component. This base component provides 3 blocks that can be built on. A pair of on/off signals allow you to control the up and down motion of the slider, and a numerical output lets you measure the slider's offset from its starting position. Multiple slider bases can run along the same track. The up/down speed can be configured by selecting this component with the select tool.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Down: Moves the slider in the track's down direction (indicated by the hollow arrow).

Up: Moves the slider in the track's up direction (indicated by the filled arrow).

Slider Position: The measured offset of the slider from its starting position.

Electric: Electrical power connection.

RPS: Power connection for transfering mechanical energy.

Fluid: Fluid connection for transfering fluid.

families.title: Liquid-Liquid Heat Exchanger
families.summary: Exchanges heat between two liquid systems in 2x2 and 5x5 variants.
families.body: A liquid-liquid heat exchanger transfers heat between two liquid circuits, bringing their temperatures toward one another. Heat exchange is described as proportional to component size. The family has 2x2 and 5x5 variants.

sections.title: Connections and temperature outputs
sections.body: Fluid A In and Fluid A Out connect one liquid circuit. Fluid B In and Fluid B Out connect the other. Temp A and Temp B report the two compartment temperatures.

sections.title: Size variants
sections.body: The 2x2 and 5x5 variants have definition masses of 4 and 16, definition values of 30 and 50, and listed voxel counts of 4 and 25. Both have the same labelled ports and descriptions.

families.title: Modular Engine Cylinder
families.summary: Produces power on a crankshaft and shares manifolds with directly adjacent cylinders.
families.body: A cylinder attaches to a crankshaft's outer surface to produce engine power. It needs a manifold to move air, fuel and exhaust. Directly adjacent cylinders can share a manifold. Composite Data reports air volume on value 1, fuel volume on value 2 and temperature on value 3. The family has 1x1, 3x3 and 5x5 variants.

families.title: Oil Rig Well Head
families.summary: A well head for oil drilling.
families.body: Once anchored to the terrain, a drill rod can be inserted into a well head to begin drilling a well. In order to drill effectively a drill rod should be driven by a rotary table and forced downward toward the terrain. A continuous supply of drilling slurry must be provided through the drill rod via a swivel, and the saturated drilling slurry extracted from the well head fluid port.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Anchor: Extend / retract piles to anchor the well head to the terrain, allowing for a new well to be drilled. The well head must be close to the terrain (~1m) and upright (+-30 degrees) to be anchored. Unanchoring the well will reset any drilling progress made.

Is Anchored: Returns true when the well head is anchored to the terrain.

Drill Depth: Returns the depth of an attached drill rod in meters.

Well Depth: Returns the depth of the drilled well in meters.

families.title: PID Controller
families.summary: A control loop feedback mechanism that measures and corrects the error in a system over time.
families.body: It takes the current measured output of a system or sensor, and a desired target measurement. It outputs a value that can be used as an input to the system to gradually correct its error. For example, the controller could input to an engine's throttle to maintain a desired speed or altitude. The control terms (proportional, integral and derivative) can be set by selecting the component with the select tool. The control terms must be carefully tuned for optimal output.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Active: Sets whether or not the controller is active. When inactive, stored values are reset.

Control Output: The output computed by the controller.

Process Variable: The current measured value of the system.

Setpoint: The desired value to correct the process variable to.

families.title: Pilot Seat
families.summary: The pilot seat lets you translate keyboard presses into output signals that can control logic components.
families.body: It provides 4 number outputs that produce a standard value ranging from -1 to 1, and 6 on/off outputs. You can get in and out of the pilot seat by interacting with it using [$[action_use_seat]].

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Occupied: Outputs an on signal if this seat is occupied by a character.

Trigger [$[action_trigger]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_trigger]] is held, and off when it is not.

Look X: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the X-axis.

Look Y: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the Y-axis.

Axis 1 [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_left]] and [$[action_right]]. [$[action_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 2 [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_up]] and [$[action_down]]. [$[action_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_up]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 3 [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_pedal_left]] and [$[action_pedal_right]]. [$[action_pedal_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_pedal_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 4 [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_throttle_up]] and [$[action_throttle_down]]. [$[action_throttle_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_throttle_up]] moves it towards 1.

Hotkey 1 [$[action_hotkey_1]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_1]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 2 [$[action_hotkey_2]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_2]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 3 [$[action_hotkey_3]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_3]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 4 [$[action_hotkey_4]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_4]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 5 [$[action_hotkey_5]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_5]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 6 [$[action_hotkey_6]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_6]] is held, and off when it is not.

Seat data: Outputs the axis, hotkey and occupied data from the seat. (On/Off 1+ : Hotkeys) (On/Off 31 : Trigger) (On/Off 32 : Occupied) (Value 1 : [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]) (Value 2 : [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]) (Value 3 : [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]) (Value 4 : [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]) (Value 9 : Look X)  (Value 10 : Look Y)

Headset Audio: Label only; no description is supplied.

Headset Video: Displays video UI overlay on a helmet mounted display.

families.title: Pneumatic Piston
families.summary: A pneumatic piston that can be expanded and contracted.
families.body: A standard value input sets the target position that the piston rod should move to. There is also an output for taking a measurement of the rod's current position. The piston can expand by a length of 1 metre, making it a total of 2.25m (9 blocks) tall when expanded and 1.25m (5 blocks) tall when contracted. The piston's speed can be configured by selecting it with the select tool.

findings.label: Pneumatic Piston · description
findings.value: A standard value input sets the target position that the piston rod should move to. There is also an output for taking a measurement of the rod's current position. The piston can expand by a length of 1 metre, making it a total of 2.25m (9 blocks) tall when expanded and 1.25m (5 blocks) tall when contracted. The piston's speed can be configured by selecting it with the select tool.

Gimbal Input: Inputs rotation data for radar in manual mode. Value 1: The yaw angle of the radar measured in turns, Value 2: The pitch angle of the radar measured in turns from -0.125 to 0.125.

families.title: Saddle Seat
families.summary: A small padded seat with control handlebars.
families.body: You can get in and out of the seat by interacting with it using [$[action_use_seat]]. You can place a rescued survivor in any seat by using [$[action_use_seat]] while carrying them.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Occupied: Outputs an on signal if the seat is occupied by a character.

Trigger [$[action_trigger]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_trigger]] is held, and off when it is not.

Look X: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the X-axis.

Look Y: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the Y-axis.

Axis 1 [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_left]] and [$[action_right]]. [$[action_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 2 [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_up]] and [$[action_down]]. [$[action_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_up]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 3 [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_pedal_left]] and [$[action_pedal_right]]. [$[action_pedal_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_pedal_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 4 [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_throttle_up]] and [$[action_throttle_down]]. [$[action_throttle_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_throttle_up]] moves it towards 1.

Hotkey 1 [$[action_hotkey_1]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_1]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 2 [$[action_hotkey_2]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_2]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 3 [$[action_hotkey_3]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_3]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 4 [$[action_hotkey_4]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_4]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 5 [$[action_hotkey_5]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_5]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 6 [$[action_hotkey_6]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_6]] is held, and off when it is not.

Seat data: Outputs the axis, hotkey and occupied data from the seat. (On/Off 1+ : Hotkeys) (On/Off 31 : Trigger) (On/Off 32 : Occupied) (Value 1 : [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]) (Value 2 : [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]) (Value 3 : [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]) (Value 4 : [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]) (Value 9 : Look X)  (Value 10 : Look Y)

Headset Audio: Label only; no description is supplied.

Headset Video: Displays video UI overlay on a helmet mounted display.

families.title: Sonar (Large)
families.summary: A sonar that returns information about a detected objects within 200km.
families.body: This sensor outputs the relative angle to detected objects within its range using underwater sound waves. The sensor will passively detect certain noisy components such as propellers or engines but can also send out a loud ping to detect quiet underwater bodies. While the ping input is held passive signals will be supressed. After activating a ping additional detected signals will appear momentarily in the data channel as the signal returns to the sonar. Activating another ping will override the previous ping and no further data will be returned from the old signal.

Sonar Data: Outputs data for up to 16 targets. On/Off 1-16 : Target 1 Found, Target 2 Found, Etc... Values 1-32: Target 1 Pivot, Target 1 Pitch, Target 2 Pivot, Target 2 Pitch, Etc...

findings.label: Sonar (Small) · description
findings.value: This sensor outputs the relative angle to detected objects within its range using underwater sound waves. The sensor will passively detect certain noisy components such as propellers or engines but can also send out a loud ping to detect quiet underwater bodies. While the ping input is held passive signals will be supressed. After activating a ping additional detected signals will appear momentarily in the data channel as the signal returns to the sonar. Activating another ping will override the previous ping and no further data will be returned from the old signal.

families.title: Space Seat
families.summary: The space seat lets you translate keyboard presses into output signals that can control logic components.
families.body: It provides 4 number outputs that produce a standard value ranging from -1 to 1, and 6 on/off outputs. You can get in and out of the space seat by interacting with it using [$[action_use_seat]].

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
Occupied: Outputs an on signal if the handle is occupied by a character.

Trigger [$[action_trigger]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_trigger]] is held, and off when it is not.

Look X: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the X-axis.

Look Y: Outputs the character look direction in turns along the Y-axis.

Axis 1 [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_left]] and [$[action_right]]. [$[action_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 2 [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_up]] and [$[action_down]]. [$[action_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_up]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 3 [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_pedal_left]] and [$[action_pedal_right]]. [$[action_pedal_left]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_pedal_right]] moves it towards 1.

Axis 4 [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]: Outputs a standard value between -1 and 1, controlled using [$[action_throttle_up]] and [$[action_throttle_down]]. [$[action_throttle_down]] causes the output value to move towards -1, and [$[action_throttle_up]] moves it towards 1.

Hotkey 1 [$[action_hotkey_1]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_1]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 2 [$[action_hotkey_2]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_2]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 3 [$[action_hotkey_3]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_3]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 4 [$[action_hotkey_4]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_4]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 5 [$[action_hotkey_5]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_5]] is held, and off when it is not.

Hotkey 6 [$[action_hotkey_6]]: Outputs an on signal when [$[action_hotkey_6]] is held, and off when it is not.

Seat data: Outputs the axis, hotkey and occupied data from the helm. (On/Off 1+ : Hotkeys) (On/Off 31 : Trigger) (On/Off 32 : Occupied) (Value 1 : [$[action_left]]/[$[action_right]]) (Value 2 : [$[action_up]]/[$[action_down]]) (Value 3 : [$[action_pedal_left]]/[$[action_pedal_right]]) (Value 4 : [$[action_throttle_up]]/[$[action_throttle_down]]) (Value 9 : Look X)  (Value 10 : Look Y)

Headset Audio: Label only; no description is supplied.

Headset Video: Displays video UI overlay on a helmet mounted display.

Fluid In: Label only; no description is supplied.

families.title: Torque Connector
families.summary: A small torque connector that can be used to transfer mechanical energy between vehicles.
families.body: Two torque connectors will attach when they are within close proximity. When connected, mechanical energy will be transferred between the connectors.

families.title: Xor
families.summary: A logic gate that outputs the logical XOR of two input signals.
families.body: The output will be switched on if only one of the signals are on. The output will be switched off if the two signals are the same.

sections.title: Documented connections
sections.body:
A: The first value to perform the logical XOR on.

B: The first value to perform the logical XOR on.

A XOR B: Outputs an on signal if only A is on, or only B is on. The output is off if A and B are both on or off.
